title: Correlative Light Electron Microscopy (CLEM) for Tracking and Imaging Viral Protein Associated Structures in Cryo-immobilized Cells
protocol: Transfer patterned sapphire discs into a 15 mL conical centrifugation tube.
Wash patterned sapphire discs thoroughly with ethanol.
Spread patterned sapphire discs in a Petri dish on filter paper and let them dry.
Place patterned sapphire discs on a glass slide using slim long tweezers.
Check the pattern of coordinates on each sapphire disc with an inverted microscope at 4X magnification.
Flip sapphire discs if necessary to ensure the pattern is readable.
Store patterned sapphire discs in a Petri dish.
Sterilize patterned sapphire discs with an ultraviolet (UV) crosslinker for 5 min.
Take sterilized patterned sapphire discs to the cell culture biosafety cabinet.
Sterilize long tweezers with ethanol in the biosafety cabinet.
Add half of the cell culture medium to a cell culture dish.
Transfer patterned sapphire discs carefully into the cell culture dish using the long tweezers.
Seed 1 x 10^5 Huh7-Lunet cells onto the culture dish.
Calculate the number of cells to ensure confluency does not exceed 20-30% at the end point of the experiment.
Check that sapphire discs remain at the bottom of the culture dish and are readable with an inverted microscope.
Push floating sapphire discs back to the correct orientation using long tweezers if necessary.
Transfect cells the next day following previously reported methods and manufacturer instructions for transfection agent.
Transfer sapphire discs to a metal imaging plate containing 30-50 μL of pH indicator-free medium at the end point of the experiment.
Image the cells under an inverted widefield fluorescence microscope.
Acquire first a low magnification image (10–20X) of the cells to allocate cells expressing FPs.
Record the coordinates of the patterned sapphire discs where the cells of interest are located by using differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy.

Acquire high magnification (fluorescence and DIC) images (63–100X, oil-immersion objectives) of the same cell/cells to better discern the subcellular localization of the protein of interest within the intracellular space.
Place the "A" and "B" aluminum carriers for HPF in a Petri dish with filter paper soaked with 1-hexadecene.
Immerse the patterned sapphire discs containing the cells in a Petri dish with 1-hexadecene.
Move the patterned sapphire discs to wash away the cell culture medium.
Place a "B" carrier with its flat side upwards on the bottom of the HPF holder.
Position the patterned sapphire discs on the flat side of the "B" carrier, cells facing upwards.
Add an "A" carrier with its 0.1-mm depth side facing the cells.
Alternatively, use a special aluminum carrier designed for the patterned sapphire disc directly on top if available.
Close the holder of the HPF machine.
Freeze the cells in the holder.
Use safety goggles and hearing protection headset.
Place the frozen "sandwich" in a polystyrene box with liquid nitrogen for temporary storage.
Place each "sandwich" in a separate 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tube marked with a number inside the polystyrene box.
Store samples in cryo-tubes with a hole punched in the top, held in a rack in a cryogenic liquid nitrogen dewar located in a room with oxygen gas sensors.
Work in a biosafety cabinet for all procedures.
Read the Material Safety Data Sheets provided by manufacturers carefully.
Consult local safety officers about safe handling rules.
Follow local institute’s health and safety procedures for equipment use and waste disposal.
Cut an "A" carrier from its deeper side to 0.2 mm thickness reducing it to 0.05 mm.
Place a patterned sapphire disc with alphanumeric etchings on the flat side of a "B" carrier, cells facing upwards.
Position a modified "A" carrier (with 0.1-mm depth) atop the sapphire disc in the "B" carrier to complete the HPF assembly.
Fill up the FS machine with liquid nitrogen.
Set the temperature to -90 °C and wait until it reaches this temperature.
Prepare the FS medium containing 0.2% osmium tetroxide (v/v) and 0.1% uranyl acetate (w/v) in glass-distilled acetone while the machine is cooling down.
Mix 600 μL of 4% OsO4 with 0.012 g of UA in a small glass container.
Dissolve this mixture in an ultrasonic bath for 5 minutes.
Add 11.4 mL of glass-distilled acetone to the mixture and mix well.
Fill microcentrifuge tubes with 200-500 μL of FS medium, close the lids, and transfer them to the FS machine.
Wait 10 minutes for the FS medium to cool down.
Transfer frozen "sandwiches" containing sapphire discs with cells using cooled long tweezers into the microcentrifuge tubes filled with FS medium.
Run the freeze substitution process from -90 °C to -80 °C for 8 hours.
Continue the process from -80 °C to -50 °C for 8 hours.
Proceed from -50 °C to -20 °C for 2 hours.
Finally, run from -20 °C to 0 °C for 2 hours.
Take out substituted specimens from the FS machine and place them on ice for 20 min.
Keep samples at room temperature for 20 min.
Wash samples thoroughly (3 times, 10 min each) with glass-distilled acetone.
Discard aluminum carriers with long tweezers if they are still in the microcentrifuge tubes after the FS.
Infiltrate cells on sapphire discs in a four-step epoxy resin series using 1 h incubations in 25%, 50%, and 75% resin in glass-distilled acetone, followed by overnight incubation with 100% resin.
Exchange 100% resin the next day for 1h.
Carefully place sapphire discs into flow-through rings mounted in reagent baths filled with 100% resin.
Push the sapphire discs completely to the bottom with coordinates facing upwards.
Check the positioning of the sapphire discs using a binocular attached to a fume extractor or a binocular inside a biosafety cabinet.
Label the samples by including a paper tag in the resin block if necessary.
Polymerize the samples in the oven at 60 °C for 48 hours.
Remove the hard resin blocks containing the cells from the oven and let them cool to room temperature before cutting.
Cut the embedding molds with a razor blade to access the resin blocks.
Remove the cylindrical resin blocks using tweezers.
Number the blocks with a permanent marker if not already labeled, and store them in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Immerse the tip of the resin block containing the sapphire disc in liquid nitrogen until it stops bubbling.
Immerse the tip of the resin block in boiling H2O.
Repeat the two previous steps as many times as needed until the sapphire disc falls off of the resin block.
Identify the area on the resin block face where the cells of interest are present by examining the block face with the binocular of an ultramicrotome.
Trim the embedded cell monolayer containing the cell/cells of interest to a small flat pyramid with the shape of a trapezium (~ 200 µm × 250 µm average size) with a clean razor blade.
Obtain 70-nm ultrathin sections of the embedded cells with a 35° diamond knife.
Place the sections on EM slot grids with help of ultra-fine tweezers.
Store the grids in a grid box.
Place the slot grid into the holder of the transmission electron microscope.
Acquire low magnification (overview) images where the complete cell profile is visible.
Find the cell/cells of interest by using the cell profiles and locations from DIC views acquired before by LM.
Acquire high magnification images of the cell/cells of interest to find ultrastructural features corresponding to fluorescent signals observed previously by LM.
Obtain montage images at high magnification for an overview at high resolution of the cell/cells of interest.
Acquire images of the same cell in consecutive serial sections to reconstruct the cell in 3D before comparing to fluorescence images.
